mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2.0% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes and preemptively discount future cash flows, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in any month where CPIAUCSL > 2.0% and FEDFUNDS < previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% signals wage stickiness and increased labor market tightness, which is associated with stronger corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 0.5% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are negative in all months where PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in monthly INDPRO supply index below 90 triggers a supply-side shock that reduces future production capacity, elevating equity risk premia and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 90 in a month
failure_condition: In months with INDPRO < 90, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST retail sales and RSAFS industrial production below trend levels for two consecutive months indicates weakening aggregate demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < trend and RSAFS < trend for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in any month meeting the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.25% for three consecutive months, the expected path of discount rates rises, depressing the present value of future equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4.0% in a month accompanied by a rise in PAYEMS above 2.0% suggests a shift from labor market tightness to slack, reducing earnings growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% and PAYEMS rises above 2.0% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in all months satisfying the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 consumer demand index below 110 for four consecutive quarters is interpreted as a structural softening in economic activity, elevating risk aversion and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 meets the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%), the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 demand exceeds 135, signaling a sustained accommodative stance that supports equity valuation expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month GDPC1 MA > 135 AND FEDFUNDS < 2.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in any qualifying month (p > 0.05).
